Change has been successfully merged
Please log a message to journal here as it is an error scenario. "i_fruThreadContext" should not be null at this point.
Acknowledged, updated

Scope can be reduced as it is being used only at one place. 
The object can be instantiate in place. for reference, We are using that in gpio_monitor.cpp
Done

Throwing from here will need better handing at the caller end as it will break the while loop as well.
Throwing from a detached thread etc just adds complexity.
Is it possible to have a less complex approach here as this situation will most likely never happen.

Why not return an empty string from here and in case of empty string by pass launching the thread and just reduce the FRU count.

I think throwing is the better approach,
1. Makes the impossible visible — logged in the catch block of caller processFruCollection with the chassis path for diagnostics.
2. Keeps normal and error semantics distinct — an empty return from getNextFruPath should mean "iterator exhausted", not "something went wrong".

The subsequent commit, m_frusCount cleanup will takes place for any pending FRUs for the chassis whose VPD collection is not triggered from the caller processFruCollection API.

I don't see any impossible being visible only by throwing and not returning empty string, so actually I don't buy that.
Having said that, 

There are few downsides that I see in the throw implementation.

(a)
The throw will cause the code to crash as per current implementation.


The code throws from here when "i_fruThreadContext" is null. The call reaches catch, there the code is calling "m_chassisEeepromPath" using "i_fruThreadContext" which is actually null. This will not work.

(b)
Though this is low priority concern, If it breaks somewhere in between, then because of throw we loose one complete thread from the pool assigned to that chassis.
as discussed, updated the code

> Enable concurrent FRU VPD

The commit header says "parallel". There is a difference between "parallel" and "concurrent". Please specify which approach this commit follows.
Done

There should be a check for zero before decrementing the counter. Since `m_frusCount` is a `size_t`, if its decremented below 0, it can underflow to `SIZE_MAX` which can be catastrophic and deadlock the `processChassisResults()` infinite loop.
added check in the caller before updating m_frusCount.

I think each API should handle it's own checks independently. If in any future refactoring, `launchFruCollectionPool()` called from some other place and the caller misses the zero check, we can hit this underflow.

I think we should still have checks wherever the counter is being decremented since the impact can be catastrophic and debugging such underflow issues can be challenging.
done
`l_errCode` is declared once and reused across loop iterations. If collectFruVpd sets it on FRU #1 and FRU #2 runs without resetting it, the error code from FRU #1 bleeds into FRU #2's context

l_errCode used for calling collectFruVpd, since the API is setting it to Zero before accessing it, its safe to use across FRU VPD collection.

to reduce the scope, am moving declaration down.
Missing `l_errCode` check.
we are not processing VPD collection result here, hence not validating the outcome.
Then how and where it will be logged? Won't we loose what failure was returned by collectFruVpd in the process of collecting the FRU? @anupama.b.r1@ibm.com
collectFruVpd has a log for failure scenario, it will be a duplicate log here.

No it does not handles all the scenario. 
Lets take up logging in the flow as a separate commit. For now, I am ok with the current change.

There should be a check for zero before decrementing the counter. Since `m_frusCount` is a `size_t`, if its decremented below 0, it can underflow to `SIZE_MAX` which can be catastrophic and deadlock the `processChassisResults()` infinite loop.
m_frusCount is incremented with FRUs size, unless if this variable is decremented twice, the situation will never occur. Hence validating is not required.

Should we have a check of "<=0" instead of just "!=0" it will take care of any movement to negative due to any corner case. I don't see any downside there.
Also in that case the extra check for fru size will not be handled.

As mentioned, to be in safer side, added the check.
checking > 0 is sufficient before decrementing it. so added this change.
The wrapping does not looks correct, its way before 72nd character.
Done
If we have check of "<=0" then we can avoid this code and it will handle the case where values can go to negative due to some corner cases.
minimum motherboard will be there for an chassis, so checking for <=1
Acknowledged
A blank line between blocks of code.
Done

A patch set should be complete in itself. Should not leave known loop holes. I don't see a reason why "m_frusCount" can't be handled in this commit itself as merging this commit without that leaves a potential defect where m_frusCount may never reach 0.
as discusses, updated the code.
Same as above.
Acknowledged
Suggestion: A comment explaining this loop can be useful. We can also simplify this using `std::find_if` and eliminate this loop, the `continue` and the `break` statement.
will the API name and doxygen for the API is not sufficient to understand what the api is doing ?

I don't see any significant efficiency improvement by using std::find_if compared with the existing implementation in this scenario.
 So keeping the existing implementation.
Acknowledged
